scoutNotes: The PR adds a currency column after amountCents to the account-transfer CSV header and fills each row from the exported account's currency. It updates the route documentation and adds an HTTP integration test using an NZD transfer with a quoted memo.

confirmed.title: Bare carriage returns split CSV rows
confirmed.rootCause: The CSV encoder does not quote fields containing a lone carriage return, so an allowed memo can corrupt the exported record structure.
confirmed.summary: The CSV encoder does not quote fields containing a lone carriage return, so an allowed memo can corrupt the exported record structure.
confirmed.failure: A valid transfer whose memo is "first\rsecond" exports an unquoted carriage return. A standard CSV reader splits that transfer into a six-column row ending at "first" and a two-column row beginning with "second", corrupting the record structure.

sites.title: Bare carriage returns split CSV rows

confirmed.reasoning: Confirmed end to end through the HTTP API. POST /transfers accepted memo "first\rsecond" with status 201 and preserved the carriage return; POST /accounts/:id/export returned 200. src/export.js quotes only fields matching /[",\n]/, so the resulting CSV contained AUD,first\rsecond without quotes. Python's csv.reader parsed it as a six-field transfer row followed by a two-field row rather than one seven-field row. The full test suite passed, but no test covers a lone carriage return. HEAD^ has the same csvCell implementation, confirming the defect is pre-existing rather than introduced by this diff.

missed.why: The tests split the contract across cases: the empty-export test checks only the header, while the currency-value test always creates a transfer.
